title: FITS DATE-OBS records the END of the exposure, not the start - off by exactly EXPTIME
what_happened: 30 s exposure: native log 'Starting 30s exposure' at 14:04:37.85, 'Exposure complete' at 14:05:09.05; the FITS says DATE-OBS = '2026-08-01T14:05:09.000Z'. 5 s exposure: start 14:07:56.16, complete 14:08:01.93, DATE-OBS = '2026-08-01T14:08:01.000Z'. In both cases DATE-OBS equals the completion timestamp, i.e. it is late by exactly the exposure duration. The Dart side takes `capturedImage.timestamp` (the download/completion time returned by the bridge) and hands it straight to FitsWriteHeader.captureTimestamp, even though the same function already holds `exposureStartedAt`.
expected: DATE-OBS is the start of the observation by FITS convention (and is what every photometry/occultation/astrometry tool assumes). It should have been 14:04:37 and 14:07:56 respectively.
repro: 1. Imaging, set exposure 30, Snapshot. 2. `grep 'Starting\|Exposure complete' /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/app.log`. 3. Dump DATE-OBS from the written FITS. 4. Repeat with exposure 5 - the error scales with the duration, proving it is end-of-exposure and not clock skew.
evidence: app.log: `14:04:37.849660 Starting 30s exposure` / `14:05:09.054820 Exposure complete`; FITS header `DATE-OBS= '2026-08-01T14:05:09.000Z'` with `EXPTIME = 30.0`. Second pair: `14:07:56.164360 Starting 5s exposure` / `14:08:01.926435 Exposure complete`, `DATE-OBS= '2026-08-01T14:08:01.000Z'`, `EXPTIME = 5.0`.
proposed_fix: Pass `exposureStartedAt` (already in scope at imaging_service.dart) as the FITS captureTimestamp and keep the download time only for captured_images.captured_at. Add DATE-END or EXPEND if the completion time is wanted. Note the sequencer path has the same bug at api/imaging.rs:3383 where capture_timestamp is `chrono::Utc::now()` at header-build time.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced across three different durations in my own log/FITS pairs. 20 s: 'Starting 20s exposure' 15:21:34.986, 'Exposure complete' 15:21:55.903, DATE-OBS='2026-08-01T15:21:55.000Z'. 30 s: start 15:40:36.034, complete 15:41:07.261, DATE-OBS=15:41:07. 3 s: start 15:37:39.198, complete 15:37:42.998, DATE-OBS=15:37:42. In every case DATE-OBS equals the completion instant, so the error scales exactly with EXPTIME (rules out clock skew). Chain confirmed in source: the sim path sets `timestamp: chrono::Utc::now()` when it builds CapturedImageResult after the exposure loop (api/imaging.rs ~line 855); imaging_service.dart:326 does `captureTimestamp = parseUtcTimestamp(capturedImage.timestamp)` while `exposureStartedAt` is already in scope a few lines below; persistence.dart:49 passes it as FitsWriteHeader.captureTimestamp; the writer emits it as DATE-OBS. The footnote about the sequencer is also correct and arguably worse: FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context (api/imaging.rs:3384) hardcodes `capture_timestamp: chrono::Utc::now()` at header-build time, i.e. after download. Severity left at P0: it is silent, systematic, affects every frame from both paths, and invalidates any timing-sensitive science.

title: Framing screen reports the wrong sensor size (1920x1080) for a camera that delivers 4144x2822 - the FOV rectangle is less than half the true width
what_happened: Framing sidebar shows 'Sensor 1920 x 1080', 'FOV 0.78 x 0.44 deg', 'Resolution 1.46 arcsec/px', and the OPTICAL CONFIG overlay repeats '1920 x 1080 px (3.76um)'. The same connected camera in the same app session delivers 4144 x 2822 frames: the Imaging toolbar reads '4144 x 2822', the written FITS has NAXIS1=4144/NAXIS2=2822, and each file is 23,394,240 bytes = 4144*2822*2 + header. At 1.4632 arcsec/px the true FOV is 1.68 x 1.15 deg, so the FOV box drawn over the DSS2 imagery is 2.16x too narrow. A user composing a mosaic or checking whether a target fits would get it badly wrong.
expected: The Framing FOV must be computed from the same sensor geometry the camera actually delivers. Two surfaces of one app must not disagree about one connected camera.
repro: 1. Connect the sim camera. 2. Imaging -> Snapshot -> note '4144 x 2822' in the toolbar and NAXIS1/2 in the FITS. 3. Plan Tonight -> Framing (Send to Framing from any target). 4. Read Sensor/FOV in the sidebar.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-106-addseq.png (OPTICAL CONFIG: 'Simulated Camera / 1920 x 1080 px (3.76um) / FOV 0.78 x 0.44 / Scale 1.46"/px'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-31-done.png (toolbar '4144 x 2822'), FITS header NAXIS1=4144 NAXIS2=2822
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/framing_provider/support.dart:107-109 (pixelsX = status.sensorWidth from backend.getCameraStatus) vs native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sim_frame.rs:41-42 (SIM_W=1920, SIM_H=1080) and native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/devices/simulation.rs:68-69
proposed_fix: Two parts. (a) Finish the unification sim_frame.rs:33-41 claims to have done - the manual-capture path still produces 4144x2822 while status advertises 1920x1080, so 'the frame a caller receives matches the geometry the camera advertised' is currently false. (b) Independently, have the framing FOV cross-check the advertised geometry against the last delivered frame and warn instead of silently drawing a wrong box - on real ASCOM hardware the same split exists between CameraXSize and an active subframe/ROI.
verdict_reasoning: The contradiction reproduces exactly: the Framing sidebar reads 'Sensor 1920 x 1080 / FOV 0.78 x 0.44 / Resolution 1.46 arcsec/px' while the Imaging toolbar reads '4144 x 2822' and every written FITS has NAXIS1=4144 NAXIS2=2822 at 23,394,240 bytes. Third data point I collected: the autofocus path logs '[SEQ] Autofocus point N sample 1/1 completed: 1920x1080 (2073600 pixels)', so two of three paths use 1920x1080 and only manual capture uses 4144x2822 (api/imaging.rs: `full_width = 4144 / bin_x`). sim_frame.rs:32-42 explicitly claims this was unified ('so the frame a caller receives matches the geometry the camera advertised... They previously disagreed three ways') and that claim is false. Two corrections. (a) The title's attribution is backwards: framing_provider/support.dart:100-109 faithfully uses the geometry the camera ADVERTISES (simulation.rs:68-69 sensor_width = SIM_W = 1920); the liar is the manual-capture generator. (b) It is simulator-only — on real ASCOM/INDI hardware the delivered frame matches CameraXSize — so no user with real gear gets a wrong FOV box from this. Reduced to P2 (simulator-fidelity defect, which this project does track as real work).

title: Abort capture does not actually stop the exposure - the camera runs the full duration after "Exposure cancelled"
what_happened: I started a 30 s light at 14:49:49.15, then pressed the toolbar 'Abort capture' X. The native log records 'Exposure cancelled' at 14:50:13.11 (24.0 s in) - and then 'Exposure complete' at 14:50:20.38, i.e. start + 31.2 s, the full exposure. The UI showed 'Stopping...' but the on-image progress ring kept counting to 97% / '1.0s remaining' 4 s after the cancel. The app side handles it correctly (no phantom frame: captured_images stayed at 11 rows and /tmp still had 11 files), but the camera was still integrating and still busy for 7 s after the user was told it had been cancelled. On a 600 s sub that window is ~9.5 minutes during which the app looks Idle and the user is free to slew, change filter or start another capture.
expected: Abort issues a real AbortExposure/StopExposure to the driver, the camera stops within a second, and the UI does not keep counting down a cancelled exposure.
repro: 1. Imaging, exposure 30, Snapshot. 2. After ~20 s press the X (Abort capture) in the preview toolbar. 3. `grep 'Starting\|cancelled\|complete' /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/app.log` and compare timestamps to the requested duration.
evidence: app.log: `14:49:49.146154 Starting 30s exposure` / `14:50:13.111425 Exposure cancelled` / `14:50:20.383265 Exposure complete`; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-99-abort.png (buttons read 'Stopping...' while the ring reads 97% / 1.0s remaining, 4 s after the cancel was logged)
where: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs (cancel path drops the Dart-side await instead of aborting the device exposure); packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:652 ('Abort capture')
proposed_fix: Make the cancel path call the driver's abort and only report 'cancelled' once the device reports not-exposing. Stop the progress ring the moment cancel is issued rather than letting the original timer run out.
verdict_reasoning: The timing reproduces: 'Starting 30s exposure' 15:41:49.208, 'Exposure cancelled' 15:41:57.702 (8.5 s in), 'Exposure complete' 15:42:20.425 = start + 31.2 s. Same shape at 15:26:27/15:26:37/15:26:58. So in the app as driven, cancel is cosmetic and the sim keeps integrating. BUT the stated root cause and the stated consequence are wrong, which materially changes the finding. api_camera_cancel_exposure (api/imaging.rs:1230-1244) branches on the device id: for `sim_` it only sets `camera.status.state = Idle` and logs 'Exposure cancelled' while the exposure future keeps sleeping to completion, then still publishes ExposureComplete{success:true} and stores the frame; for every real device it calls unified_device_ops::mark_camera_exposure_aborted plus DeviceManager::camera_abort_exposure, which reaches the driver's AbortExposure (real_device_ops.rs:1662-1704, device_manager/ops/camera.rs:1178-1248). The claim 'on a 600 s sub that window is ~9.5 minutes during which the camera is still integrating' therefore does not hold for real hardware — this is a simulator no-op, exactly the 'simulators fail in the pass-making direction' class. What IS real on both paths is the UI half: the progress ring keeps counting after cancel, because wait_for_camera_exposure_complete (unified_device_ops.rs:148-203) keeps publishing ExposureProgress until is_complete or the duration+margin deadline. No phantom frame was recorded (captured_images did not gain a row for either cancelled exposure). Reduced to P2.

title: The "1:1 zoom" button and the "100%" readout are fit-to-window - a 4144 px frame is shown at 987 screen px (23.8%)
what_happened: The preview opens at '100%' with the entire 4144 x 2822 frame visible inside a ~1050 x 660 viewport. I measured the rendered frame in the screenshot: it spans screen x 413..1399, i.e. 987 px wide for a 4144 px image = 23.8% actual scale, while the readout says 100%. Pressing the button whose tooltip is '1:1 zoom' returns to exactly that same view (max pixel diff 1.0 against the initial 100% render) and the readout again reads 100%. Pressing 'Fit to window' also produces 100%. So both buttons mean the same thing and neither gives a true 1:1 pixel view; a genuine 1:1 is only reachable by pressing Zoom in ~7 times (max is 800%, i.e. ~1.9x actual).
expected: 100% / 1:1 means one image pixel per screen pixel. This is what you use to judge focus, star shape, tilt and trailing - at the current 4.2x downsample those are all invisible.
repro: 1. Take a snapshot (4144 x 2822). 2. Read the zoom chip: 100%. 3. Press the '1:1 zoom' button (3rd zoom button) - still 100%, identical render. 4. Press 'Fit to window' (4th) - also 100%. 5. Measure the rendered frame width in the screenshot.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-zoom-fit.png ('4144 x 2822 | Bin 1x1 | 100%'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-100-aborted.png; measured extent x 413..1399 = 987 px, 987/4144 = 0.238; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-zoom-max.png (max zoom = 800%)
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:638 (tooltip '1:1 zoom') and 644 ('Fit to window'); the zoom factor is stored relative to fit, not to native pixels
proposed_fix: Express the zoom readout as (displayed px / image px) so fit reads ~24% and 1:1 reads 100%, and make the 1:1 button set that ratio to exactly 1. Keep 'Fit to window' as the separate control it already is.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed from source, which is unambiguous: imaging_viewer_state_provider.dart:97-99 `fitToWindow() { state = state.copyWith(zoomLevel: 1.0, panOffset: Offset.zero); }` and :104-106 `zoom1to1() { state = state.copyWith(zoomLevel: 1.0, panOffset: Offset.zero); }` — byte-identical bodies, with the comment at :101-103 admitting 'same effective state as fit on the current implementation'. The readout is `zoomLabel: '${(zoomLevel * 100).round()}%'` (imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:75) and the render path is Transform.scale(zoomLevel) over a CustomPaint whose painter does paintImage(fit: BoxFit.contain) into the viewport rect (image_display.dart:143-172), so zoomLevel 1.0 is fit-to-window and is labelled '100%'. Live state matches: the toolbar reads '4144 x 2822 | Bin 1x1 | 100%' with the whole frame inside a ~987 px-wide viewport (~24% actual). Tooltips are '1:1 zoom' at :638 and 'Fit to window' at :644 as cited. P2 is right.

title: The autofocus result overlay never auto-dismisses and follows the user onto every other screen, covering controls
what_happened: After the autofocus run finished at 14:15 a collapsed pill 'AF: HFR 2.10' appeared bottom-right. It was still on screen 23 minutes later, and it is global: it appeared on the Imaging screen, then on the Guiding screen (where it covered the Calibration card), then on Plan Tonight, then on the Framing screen (where it covered the Rotation controls and the framing-tour buttons). Clicking near its X re-EXPANDED it into a full floating 'Autofocus' window with the HFR curve, overlapping the Framing sidebar; only the window's own X closed it. On the Imaging screen the collapsed pill also sat on top of the Dither Settings 'Settle Threshold' value and the Stack panel's 'Sigma Clipping' row, hiding them.
expected: A completion toast auto-dismisses after a few seconds, or at minimum is scoped to the Imaging screen and never overlaps interactive controls.
repro: 1. Imaging -> Focus tab -> Run Autofocus, wait for completion. 2. Navigate to Guiding, Plan Tonight, Framing. The pill follows and overlaps content on each.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-40-afdone.png (14:15, appears), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-dither.png (covers 'Settle Threshold'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-70-guidingscreen.png (Guiding), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-79-plantonight.png (Plan Tonight), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-84-framing-scroll.png (expanded 'Autofocus' window over the Framing sidebar at 14:38, 23 min later)
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/focus_panel.dart (AF result overlay hosted above the router shell rather than inside the imaging route)
proposed_fix: Auto-dismiss after ~10 s, scope the overlay to the Imaging route, and make the collapsed pill's X actually dismiss instead of expanding.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced by running a real autofocus (9 points, Hyperbolic, focuser 25000 -> 25074). A collapsed 'AF: HFR 2.09' pill appeared bottom-right at 12:17 and was still on screen at 12:21 with no auto-dismiss; navigating to the Guiding screen carried it along, where it sits on top of the 'Guiding Tour' card, covering its body text and abutting the Maybe Later / Start Tour buttons — so the 'global, not scoped to the imaging route' claim holds. One sub-claim is wrong: clicking the pill's X DID dismiss it cleanly (I clicked the X at root 1720,944 and the pill was gone on the next frame); presumably the reporter's click landed on the pill body, which expands it. Severity left at P2 — it is persistent chrome overlapping interactive content on unrelated screens, but it is dismissable.

title: False zeros: guiding peak error reads 0.00" with no guider, stack metrics read 0.00 px with no stack
what_happened: Imaging -> Guiding tab with the guider Disconnected: RA RMS, Dec RMS and Total all correctly show '---', but RA Peak and Dec Peak show '0.00"'. A 0.00" peak error is a claim of perfect guiding. The same pattern is in the Stack tab with no stack in progress: 'Avg Alignment Residual 0.00 px' and 'Avg Matched Pairs 0.0' while 'Rejection Rate' correctly shows '--'. Two panels, same bug shape: uninitialised numerics rendered as real measurements.
expected: Every no-data numeric renders as '---', exactly the way RMS and Rejection Rate already do in the same cards.
repro: 1. Leave guider disconnected, no stack running. 2. Imaging -> Guiding tab: read RA Peak / Dec Peak. 3. Imaging -> Stack tab: read Avg Alignment Residual / Avg Matched Pairs.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-dither.png (RA RMS ---, Dec RMS ---, Total ---, RA Peak 0.00", Dec Peak 0.00"), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-stack.png (Avg Alignment Residual 0.00 px, Avg Matched Pairs 0.0, Rejection Rate --)
proposed_fix: Make the peak/residual/pairs fields nullable end-to-end and render null as '---' rather than defaulting them to 0.
verdict_reasoning: Seen live on my own Imaging -> Guiding tab with the guider Disconnected: RA RMS '---', Dec RMS '---', Total '---', but RA Peak '0.00"' and Dec Peak '0.00"' in the same card. Source matches: guiding_panel.dart:144-146 use `?.toStringAsFixed(2) ?? '---'` for the three RMS values, while :154-155 do `guideStats.peakRa.toStringAsFixed(2)` / `.peakDec` on non-nullable doubles that default to 0. Same shape in the Stack tab: stacking_panel.dart:527 `stats.avgMatchedPairs.toStringAsFixed(1)` and :533 `'${stats.avgAlignmentResidual.toStringAsFixed(2)} px'` are unguarded, while :554 correctly guards Rejection Rate with `stackState.lastFrameTotalPixels > 0 ? ... : '--'`. Both files render an uninitialised numeric as a measurement, and 0.00" peak error reads as perfect guiding. P2 is right.
